summary: Feed s134_double is degraded: IDS shows 25.0% one-way TCP sessions and 6.8% packet drops, both exceed thresholds and will reduce IDS detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is delivering only one direction of bidirectional flows - 25 of 100 TCP sessions are unidirectional (25.0% > 10% threshold). Likely single-sided SPAN/TAP or asymmetric routing without aggregation at the broker, so return traffic is sent to a different tool port or dropped.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and stateful signatures. One-way visibility breaks handshake/stream reconstruction, causes false negatives and missed intrusions.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session to the same IDS tool port to restore full bidirectional flows required for stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: SPAN/mirror source is dropping packets under load - 87 of 1280 TCP packets show missing data (6.8% > 1% threshold). Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is upstream of the tool, typical of SPAN oversubscription/buffer exhaustion, not IDS overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with needs_full_payload=true misses payload segments, breaking signature matching, file reassembly and allowing evasion via dropped packets.

recommended_fix.why: Passive TAP delivers complete traffic without SPAN buffer drops, eliminating the 6.8% loss before the packet broker and IDS.
